$comment: Modelog rate table. Base rates are USD per 1M tokens, transcribed from the published card. Every MULTIPLIER is an integer ratio over ratio_scale - never a decimal - because chained float multipliers produce artefacts at table-build time (3.0 * 0.1 = 0.30000000000000004). See PRD 8.2.
$effective_date_comment: The OLDER of this file's two verification dates, by design: this field only drives a staleness check, and the Anthropic entries (verified 2026-09-27) are the ones actually that old. Using the OpenAI entries' later date (2026-10-09) here would overstate how recently the Anthropic entries were checked.
source: Anthropic first-party API list pricing (platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing, verified 2026-09-27) and OpenAI first-party API list pricing (developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing, developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol, developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6-astra, verified 2026-10-09)

cache_multipliers.$comment: Ratios over ratio_scale, applied to the model's base input rate. A model may override cache_read; the published card sets it per-model. cache_write_5m (1.25x) is also what OpenAI publishes for GPT-6 Astra ($12.50 vs $10.00 input) and GPT-6.1 Sol ($2.50 vs $2.00 input) cache writes - confirmed, not an accidental reuse of Anthropic's number. Codex's adapter always reports cache writes into the 5m bucket (OpenAI states no TTL tier), so cache_write_1h never applies to it.

modifiers.$comment: Request-level repricing, recorded per turn in message.usage. Ratios over ratio_scale, applied to EVERY token class. A value absent from these tables is UNKNOWN and must yield a null cost - see unknown_modifier_policy. Codex's service_tier shares this table under its own value names ("default", not "standard") rather than a separate field, since the role is identical: a request-level modifier the source reports per turn. Only "default" (confirmed against real captured sessions, ratio 1x) is listed - Codex also offers faster, more expensive tiers (OpenAI's own material describes a 2x-priced "Fast" mode for GPT-6 Astra and a 6x-priced "Ultrafast" mode for GPT-6.1 Sol), but the exact wire value service_tier carries for those has not been confirmed against a real log, so turns on them correctly price as unavailable rather than guessed - see unknown_modifier_policy.

$policy_note: An unrecognised model id OR an unrecognised modifier value must surface as 'cost unavailable' for that turn, never fall back to a default rate or a neutral ratio. A fast-mode turn priced at standard rates is a KNOWN model with a WRONG rate - the same confidently-wrong number the model policy exists to prevent, reached through a different door.
